source.quote: Evaluating GPT-4V + Refusal System against screenshots of a text refusal dataset finds that the combination of model-level mitigations and our refusal system enabled us to reach our internal target of a 100% refusal rate.

testers.name: Be My Eyes
testers.scope: Blind and low-vision pilot of Be My AI using GPT-4V for image descriptions and safety learnings

source.quote: Beginning in March, 2023, Be My Eyes and OpenAI collaborated to develop Be My AI, a new tool to describe the visual world for people who are blind or have low vision.

findings.text: Document is dated September 25, 2023; training of GPT-4V was completed in 2022 with early access from March 2023.

source.quote: Similar to GPT-4, training of GPT-4V was completed in 2022 and we began providing early access to the system in March 2023.

findings.text: Be My Eyes warns users not to rely on Be My AI for safety and health tasks such as reading prescriptions or checking allergens.

source.quote: Be My Eyes warns its testers and future users not to rely on Be My AI for safety and health issues like reading prescriptions, checking ingredient lists for allergens, or crossing the street.

findings.text: OpenAI does not consider this GPT-4V version fit for any medical function or as a substitute for professional medical advice.

source.quote: we do not consider the current version of GPT-4V to be fit for performing any medical function or substituting professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment, or judgment.

findings.text: The model can give incorrect instructions to synthesize a dangerous compound such as Isotonitazene.

source.quote: the model would give information for the synthesis and analysis of some dangerous chemicals such as Isotonitazene, a synthetic opioid.

findings.text: GPT-4V inherits GPT-4 assessments for chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN), weapons, system interaction, and self-replication; image input was not a key focus there.

source.quote: GPT-4V inherits the assessment in those areas, but this was not a key focus area as image input does not meaningfully alter the capabilities for these categories.

findings.text: Image input order can change recommendations; red teamers saw the first flag favored when ordering was swapped.

source.quote: asking for which state to move to, based on the flags inputted, favors the first flag inputted when red teamers tested both possible orderings of the flags.

findings.text: Hate-symbol handling is inconsistent; lesser-known names or symbols can bypass refusals that work for well-known groups.

source.quote: if a user directly names a well-known hate group, the model usually refuses to provide a completion. But, if you use lesser-known names–such as “Totenwaffen”–or symbols, you might get past this.

findings.text: System-level optical character recognition (OCR) plus moderation scores is used on overlaid text in images to block adversarial text-in-image prompts.

source.quote: we run images through an OCR tool and then calculate moderation scores on the resulting text in the image.
